Text: ArrayList grows its capacity by {{c1::1.5}}x when it exceeds its size limit.
Extra: Growing by 1.5x avoids excessive memory waste and bounds resizing frequency.

Text: Under the hood, ArrayList resizing delegates to {{c1::System.arraycopy()}} to move elements to the new array.
Extra: This is a native JVM operation that is highly optimized.

Text: A HashMap keys contract states: if `a.equals(b)` is true, then `a.hashCode() {{c1::==}} b.hashCode()` must be true.
Extra: If this contract is violated, key lookup fails because the map searches in the wrong bucket.

Text: TreeSet and TreeMap rely on {{c1::Comparable}} or {{c2::Comparator}} to detect duplicates and order elements.
Extra: TreeSet completely ignores equals() and hashCode() for duplicate detection.

Text: If `compareTo()` returns {{c1::0}} for two distinct objects in a TreeSet, the second object will be rejected.
Extra: A comparison result of 0 is treated by the Red-Black tree as a duplicate entry.

Text: ConcurrentHashMap uses {{c1::Compare-And-Swap (CAS)}} to write to empty buckets without locking.
Extra: If the bucket is not empty, it locks the head node of that bucket using a synchronized block.

Text: ConcurrentHashMap locks only the {{c1::head}} node of a bucket when resolving write collisions.
Extra: This bucket-level locking allows other threads to write to different buckets concurrently.

Text: Fail-fast iterators throw {{c1::ConcurrentModificationException}} if structural modifications are detected.
Extra: It detects this by comparing the collection's live modCount with the iterator's expectedModCount.

Text: The iterator for CopyOnWriteArrayList operates on a {{c1::snapshot}} of the array.
Extra: This snapshot does not change when elements are added or removed, preventing modification conflicts.

Text: `Collections.unmodifiableList()` returns an unmodifiable {{c1::view}}, meaning changes to the backing list are still visible through it.
Extra: Contrast this with List.copyOf(), which returns a fully isolated immutable list.

Text: `List.copyOf()` returns a fully {{c1::immutable}} collection that does not reference any original backing array.
Extra: It creates a new, isolated array structure holding the copied elements.

Text: Standard iterators check for modification by comparing {{c1::modCount}} with {{c2::expectedModCount}}.
Extra: Any mismatch triggers a ConcurrentModificationException immediately.
